ruling.recommended_action: Close the case: the fixed RydeX fare ($30.24) stands, no refund is due, and no account action is taken against the driver.
ruling.reasoning:
The trip was a RydeX fixed-quote booking: the fare was quoted for the Toa Payoh HDB Hub → VivoCity trip and the billed distance (13.9 km) did not exceed the optimal route, so the +3.25 km off-route segment did not enter the fare and no extra charge was collected for it [F4][F6][RD-2]. The only off-route segment is F3 (08:37–08:45, 5.14 km driven vs 1.89 km optimal, +3.25 km), and no incident on the replaced stretch is recorded (no traffic incidents near the route; band data alone does not exempt) [F3][F14][RD-4].

RD-3 does not apply: no stop was measured in that segment and the rider named no place to stop, so there is no rider-named stop to exempt (or to charge) [F3][RD-3].

Consent (RD-5) is what decides the only remaining consequence. Before the segment started, the driver asked "ok if I go round via Balestier Road?" at 08:34 and the rider answered "Sure, your call." [F7][F8]. The rider's reply is a specific approval of the route the driver proposed, sent before the 08:37 segment, and the complete chat record (2 messages, all timestamped) contains no withdrawal or narrowing of it [F9][RD-5]. The driver's after-the-fact statement to the same effect is not relied on, because a driver's own assertion of agreement is not consent; the rider's own chat message is [F10][RD-5]. On that reading the segment's extra km are not a detour for which the driver is answerable [RD-5]. The trace flags that nothing in the fact table ties the driven path to Balestier Road by road name, which is the G13 situation; but since RydeX is a fixed fare, that reading changes no amount [F4][F6][RD-2]. It changes only the RD-6 question (whether a non-exempt segment exists at all → account flag), and because the rider's own pre-segment message approves the proposed route, I do not find a non-exempt segment, so no flag is warranted; on a matter this narrow I prefer the reading that produces no adverse account action [F17][RD-6].

The fare itself contains only published items — base $3.90, distance $19.54, time $5.33, waiting $0.00, platform $1.47, no surge, no discount — so nothing is refundable under FARE-1; and no cancellation or waiting fee is disputed (waiting $0.00), so NS-6 is not triggered [F5][F6][FARE-1].

Safety screen: I read the complaint, both chat messages and the driver's statement — no threats, intimidation, harassment, sexual remarks or dangerous-driving allegation (the complaint is about route length only, and "Sure, your call." is agreement, not pressure; "Traffic ahead on Central Expressway is building up" is a routing remark) [F7][F8][F10]. Safety_concern = none [SAFE-1][SAFE-2].

Evidence: the record settles what the ruling needs — a measured off-route segment, a complete timestamped chat, a fixed-fare breakdown showing the detour km never entered the fare, and profile facts [F3][F4][F6][F9][F17]. Amount: not applicable; the policy refund formula is Σ(extra_km) × (fare.distance_fare ÷ fare.distance_km) = 3.25 km × ($19.54 ÷ 13.86 km = $1.4098/km) = $4.58, but for a non-metered fixed fare that mileage-based refund is not applicable, so the recoverable amount is $0 → no_action [F3][F4][F6][RD-2].

segment_findings.reason: Before the segment began (08:37), the driver asked 'ok if I go round via Balestier Road?' at 08:34 and the rider's own message answered 'Sure, your call.' — a general authorisation of the route choice to reach the destination, sent before the segment [F7][F8][F9]. The driver's later statement is not relied on [F10] (G11). The approved route serves the destination trip, not an errand or loop of the driver's own, so the segment's extra 3.25 km are excused [F3][RD-5]. Because the service is a fixed-fare RydeX whose billed distance did not exceed the optimal route, this finding changes no amount [F4][F6][RD-2]; it removes the RD-6 account flag, since no non-exempt segment remains [F17][RD-6].
